To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The counting problem of CACQs (acyclic CQs) is #P-complete.

(1) the counting problem of acyclic CQs is tractable, (2) the counting problem is tractable for CQs of constant hypertree-width, (3) the counting problem for CQs with a constant number of variables is intractable, (4) the counting problem remains tractable for the union of a constant number of acyclic CQS, and (5) the counting problem becomes intractable for unions of a constant number acyclic CQ

the counting problem for acyclic CQs is in polynomial time, the counting problem for CQs of hypertree-width at most one is in polynomial time as well, the counting problem of acyclic CQ unions is in polynomial time and the counting problem of arbitrary CQ unions is #P-complete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the complexity of counting the answers of CQs? How does the complexity depend on the structure of the CQs? Can the complexity be reduced by considering unions of CQ?

the following problems: (i) Given a CQ, can we count the answers efficiently? (ii) Can we efficiently compute the number of distinct answers to a C.Q.? (iii) Can we efficiently count the number of distinct answer tuples of a union of CQs?

the following three main questions: (1) What is the computational complexity of counting the number of answers to a CQL (2) What is the complexity of counting the answers of unions of CQL (3) What is the relationship between the counting problem and the evaluation problem of CQL
Tractable Counting for Conjunctive Queries over Poset-Data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the counting problem for CQs of hypertree-width k is tractable for k <= 3 and intractable for k >= 5, whereas the complexity for k = 4 remains open.
counting the number of answers to CQs is intractable for CQs of arbitrary structure, while counting the number of distinct answers to CQ unions is intractable even for unions of acyclic conjunctives.
the tractability frontier of the counting problem for CQs is the class of acyclic queries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the counting problem for CQs is tractable for acyclic CQs, CQs of hypertree-width 2 and unions of CQ's of bounded hypertree width, and intractable otherwise.
the tractable fragments of counting CQs are much larger than the fragments of evaluating them, while the intractable fragments are almost the same.
, in contrast to the case of the evaluation problem, tractability of the counting problem is rare and the counting problem is often intractable even when the evaluation problem is tractable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the counting problem of a CQ can be tractable, while the evaluation problem is not.
the counting problem of conjunctive queries can be tractable even when the evaluation problem is not.
the counting problem is more robust than the evaluation problem.
